sections.heading: Glamsterdam Devnet Status
sections.summary: Devnet 8 fork transition testing with Lido and Optimism was successful; Besu investigating performance; Frames devnet for Hegota launched.
sections.body:
- Gloas fork transition testing on devnet 8 with Lido and Optimism completed successfully; devnet has been torn down.
- Besu still investigating a performance issue; improvements recently tested and being pushed.
- Frames devnet for Hegota launched yesterday.
- Geth found a bug on devnet 8 related to catchup full sync, now fixed — catching up to head will be faster.

sections.heading: Sepolia Fork Client Releases
sections.summary: Sepolia fork confirmed for October 6; most client releases expected by early next week.
sections.body:
- Sepolia fork date: October 6, confirmed on ACDC last week; already merged into client specs.
- Client release status:
  - Nethermind 2.0: released.
  - Geth: released.
  - Besu: ETA tomorrow.
  - Reth: release coming next week (likely Monday).
  - ethrex: release candidate being tested; release today or tomorrow.

sections.heading: Glamsterdam Gas Limit — 200M at Fork
sections.summary: Agreement to signal 200M gas limit at the Glamsterdam fork for Sepolia despite a new JUMPDEST attack raising execution-time concerns.
sections.body:
- Justin Traglia raised that the gas limit schedule was missing from Sepolia configs and proposed immediately signaling 200M at fork. PR: [eth-clients/sepolia#130](https://github.com/eth-clients/sepolia/pull/130).
- potuz flagged a JUMPDEST analysis attack deployed by Paweł on devnet 8 producing valid blocks taking 8–14 seconds to execute across multiple clients, well above the 6-second safety budget.
  - Attack exploits Glamsterdam's state-gas repricing making CREATE costs cheaper to pre-pay, updating an old benchmark that was found to be wrong.
  - Relevant PRs: [execution-specs#3631](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3631) and [execution-specs#3637](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3637).
  - Nico Flaig confirmed geth took 9 seconds on his server; next proposer got reorged because it couldn't process the block in time.
- potuz clarified the attack is expensive and cannot persist, but it can reorg the next proposer — a serious but bounded risk.
- Maria Silva argued the gas limit should be set at the fork because state-byte cost repricing (EIP-8037) makes the minimum usable gas limit ~150M; delaying the increase would cause base-fee volatility. Analysis shared: [ethresear.ch post](https://ethresear.ch/t/from-60m-to-200m-simulating-glamsterdam-s-fee-market/25957).
- Csaba opposed doing the increase simultaneously with the fork, preferring to separate signals, but acknowledged the reasoning.
- Ansgar Dietrichs argued testnets should be used for aggressive stress testing — being gentle on testnets risks mainnet.
- Devnet 8 machines: 8-core, 32 GB RAM, one EL+CL per machine — described as representative or slightly over-provisioned.
- Agreement: signal 200M gas limit at the Glamsterdam fork for Sepolia. Gas will still ramp up via the 1/1024 voting mechanism (~4 hours to reach target).
- Action item: write benchmark tests for the JUMPDEST attack vector before mainnet; clients (especially Nethermind) investigating optimizations.

sections.heading: CL Block and BAL Retention Windows
sections.summary: BAL retention should match CL block retention; exact window reduction deferred for async discussion on Discord.
sections.body:
- Jihoon raised three related questions: (1) reduce CL block retention period per EIP-8061's WSP change, (2) align EL history retention to match, (3) increase BAL retention to match CL block retention per Nico's PR [EIP-12347](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12347).
- Current CL block retention is 33,024 epochs (~5 months); EIP-8061 would roughly halve it to ~14,000 epochs (~2 months). The 33k value was a worst-case WSP estimate pre-8061, now considered a bug/oversight.
- BAL retention is currently ~3,000 epochs (~10x smaller than CL block retention).
- Agreement: BAL retention window should equal the CL block retention window — no dissent.
- Marius (Geth) strongly argued for a long BAL retention window: nodes offline for days need BALs to do parallel execution during catchup; without BALs, sequential execution takes 9–10 seconds per block, making catchup impossible at higher gas limits.
- potuz noted CL must serve complete blocks including BALs; if EL doesn't keep them, CL must, causing duplication — at least two CL clients currently drop EL data from their DB.
- Łukasz (Nethermind) cautioned that reducing the network retention window to ~1 month requires fully automated ERA file hosting; currently manual.
- Toni estimated storage at ~300 GiB for 33k epochs at 200M gas and 300 KiB BALs; considered overly conservative.
- potuz and Kevaundray noted CL doesn't need anything beyond the WSP; the retention should be the max of both layers.
- Decision deferred to async discussion on an ETH R&D Discord thread, owned by Kev, Jihoon, or Toni. Not blocking for Glamsterdam or testnets.

sections.heading: EIP-8304: Trustless Log Index — DFI
sections.summary: EIP-8304 confirmed DFI for Hegota; Besu and Reth unchanged; author will continue work independently.
sections.body:
- EIP-8304 (Trustless Log Index) was a default DFI candidate; Besu and Reth (Dragan) confirmed no change in their positions.
- Zsolt (author) acknowledged the decision but stated he will continue working on the project regardless, citing future synergy with trustless API use cases.
- Decision: DFI for Hegota.

sections.heading: EIP-7979: Call and Return Opcodes — CFI
sections.summary: EIP-7979 moved to CFI for Hegota with broad client support and endorsement from Solidity.
sections.body:
- Greg Colvin summarized performance measurements: interpreter with register-code compilation yields ~2x speedup; machine-code compilation ~5x; with 64-bit ops and RISC-V compilation ~50x, including ZK proving.
  - End-to-end prototype tested with Solidity, Geth, and EVM1 — all Solidity tests pass through compilation and validation.
  - EIP-8337 proposed as a natural follow-up for static code validation.
- Solidity (Radek): supportive; will implement when delivered; posted opinion on [ETH Magicians thread](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-7979-call-and-return-opcodes-for-the-evm/24615/35). Strongly favors EIP-8337 as follow-up.
- Vyper (Charles Cooper): not on call; Greg relayed he would definitely use the opcodes and sees better code generation potential.
- Reth (Dragan): supports inclusion; wants JUMPDEST analysis removed.
- Nethermind (Ben Adams): strongly supports; argues it's been deferred for ~9 years and should finally ship.
- Besu (Justin Florentine): moved from B to open to A after Solidity's endorsement.
- Geth: no representative spoke; assumed unchanged at B.
- ethrex: weak DFI, but okay if majority wants to proceed.
- Ansgar suggested leaving as PFI until strong-CFI candidates are handled, but no strong objection.
- Decision: CFI for Hegota. No opposition raised.

sections.heading: EIP-8163: Reserve EXTENSION Opcode — CFI
sections.summary: EIP-8163 moved to CFI for Hegota as a trivial no-op reservation with L2 demand from Tron, Rootstock, and Arbitrum Nitro.
sections.body:
- Piotr (Mononaut Foundation) presented evidence of demand: custom opcode experiments from Tron and Rootstock; message of support from Arbitrum Nitro team.
- The EIP reserves opcode 0xAE as a no-op on L1, guaranteeing it won't be assigned to a different function in the future.
- Besu promoted it to S tier.
- Erigon promoted it to B tier.
- Reth (Dragan): should not be DFI; C or B — easy to do, friendly to other chains.
- ethrex: C tier.
- Nethermind (Łukasz): noted the shrinking pool of 1-byte opcodes but no objection.
- Decision: CFI for Hegota.

sections.heading: EIP-8360: TCREATE Opcode — Deferred
sections.summary: TCREATE decision deferred; champions asked to engage clients before next call, with discussion tied to self-destruct deprecation.
sections.body:
- Milos (enso.build) presented TCREATE: a new opcode for ephemeral/disposable contracts (single-transaction lifetime), used by payment flows, cross-chain intents, limit orders.
  - Currently achieved via self-destruct in the same transaction, but Glamsterdam removes the gas refund, effectively making the feature ~6x more expensive.
  - ~1,000–2,000 transactions/day on Ethereum; ~10x more on BNB Chain.
- Jochem clarified: standalone EIP, no dependencies needed for Hegota; SSTORE/SLOAD behave as TSTORE/TLOAD within TCREATE context.
- Jochem argued Ethereum is effectively deprecating this feature without providing an alternative — should have been addressed in Glamsterdam.
- Marius (Geth) opposed TCREATE for Hegota: creates many new code paths for little gain.
- Ben Adams noted some self-destruct use cases covered by SETCODEFROM but not all; TCREATE could enable full self-destruct removal.
- Reth (Dragan): reasoning for DFI was similar — alternative to self-destruct needed; may be fine for Hegota but edge cases around gas/storage need examination.
- Maria Silva: decision should be coupled with self-destruct deprecation discussion; should not be DFI'd prematurely.
- Decision deferred: Milos asked to engage clients before next call; not DFI'd.

sections.heading: EIP-8368 and EIP-8372: Gas Recalibration — Left as PFI
sections.summary: Both EIPs left as PFI pending at least 30 days of mainnet Glamsterdam data before a decision.
sections.body:
- EIP-8368 (CPSB Recalibration) and EIP-8372 (Normalized State Gas Limit) are alternatives requiring mainnet Glamsterdam data.
- Maria confirmed at least 30 days of post-fork data needed.
- No objections to leaving both in PFI status with a note they may be revisited after Glamsterdam mainnet launch.

sections.heading: Highest-Rated Hegota EIPs — Batch CFI
sections.summary: Seven EIPs moved to CFI: 7906, 8250, 8272, 7668, 8253, 3298, 8131, plus the block access list byte floor EIP bundled with 8131.
sections.body:
- EIP-7906 (Transaction Assertions via State Diff Opcode): highest-rated; strong recommendation from hardware signer community (Firmware). CFI'd with no opposition.
  - Ansgar noted concern about nuanced edge cases during implementation, but agreed it's worth it.
- EIP-8250 (Keyed Nonces for Frame Transactions): no concerns raised. CFI'd.
- EIP-8272 (Recent Roots for Frame Transactions): no concerns raised. CFI'd as a batch with 8250.
- EIP-7668 (Remove Bloom Filters): Ben Adams described it as removing technical debt — calculations nobody uses, sent across the network. CFI'd.
- EIP-8253 (Bump Nonce of Zero-Nonce Storage Accounts): replacement for EIP-7610 which was DFI'd last-minute from Glamsterdam. CFI'd.
- EIP-3298 (Remove Storage-Clear Refund and Refund Cap): Erigon and ethrex had lower tiers (lower priority, not opposition). CFI'd.
- EIP-8131 (Unified Transaction Content Floor): all A or B ratings. CFI'd.
- Ansgar and Toni proposed also CFI-ing the block access list byte floor EIP (the companion data-pricing EIP), arguing both should be bundled — doing only one leaves worst-case block size unchanged.
  - Reth (Dragan): CFI appropriate; marked C due to complexity of measuring BAL items but supports the idea.
  - Decision: CFI'd.

sections.heading: SETCODEFROM (EIP-8298) — Punted to Next Call
sections.summary: SETCODEFROM discussion showed broad interest but Besu requested more time; decision deferred to next call.
sections.body:
- lightclient flagged SETCODEFROM as important; Kevaundray requested a temp check.
- CPerezz (author) explained: SETCODEFROM allows migrating an EOA to a full code/smart/post-quantum account, superseding EIP-8058. Recent PR added initcode execution support. Explainer: https://cperezz.github.io/articles/setcodefrom-account-modes/
- Ben Adams highlighted the second benefit: deploying duplicate contracts (e.g., Uniswap liquidity pools) at code-hash cost instead of full deployment cost. SETCODEFROM avoids the consensus-split risk of a hypothetical SETCODEHASH (code DB differs between snap-synced and full-synced nodes).
- Reth (Dragan): DFI reasoning was to delay code-change decisions until after frames ship, but acknowledged it's not a strong opinion and the change is small.
- Nico warned that delaying to ISTAR risks collision with post-quantum transition timeline (~end of 2028); could become an emergency fork.
- ethrex: wants SETCODEFROM CFI'd.
- Besu (Justin Florentine): currently at C tier; finding arguments compelling but requested more time.
- Decision deferred to next call per Besu's request. 10 remaining EIPs to be reviewed by clients before then.
- Nico raised EIP-8151 (related); nixo confirmed no discussion or decision on it today.
